about: The swap rule's cases: does every active swap device keep its pages off a disk? Walked by joinery_unseal/swap_linux_test.go, tests/vault/vault_health_test.php (VaultHealth::checkSwapSafe) and the agent's primitives/unseal_daemon_test.go, whose primitives/swap_rule_cases_test.json must stay byte-identical to this file. Each case builds a fixture directory DIR: swaps rows are [path, type], with @DIR@ standing for DIR; block maps a path under DIR/block (standing for /sys/block) to its contents; block_dirs are empty directories there; files are created empty. ram_only is the verdict: true for RAM-only, false for anything else; php_state is what VaultHealth::checkSwapSafe() says of a false one (unmet when it is known to reach a disk, unknown when it cannot be judged from here).

cases.name: zram with no backing device, seen from a container (in sysfs, not in /dev)
zram on a kernel without writeback (the device in sysfs, no backing_dev file)
zram writing idle pages back to a disk
zram listed but sysfs masked or empty
a swap file whose name starts with zram
a file listed as a partition whose name starts with zram, unknown to sysfs
dm-crypt found by its mapper name (a container)
a device-mapper device whose type cannot be read
a host device sysfs does not show
a plain partition (in /dev; sysfs lists partitions under their disk, not in /sys/block)
a malformed row with no type
